found.summary:
I checked every studio, gift, online and /pro page in scope on the live site (curl of https://yakircohen.com on 2026-10-02) and compared each one with the code at HEAD 0d163c8. The working tree showed no uncommitted changes when I ran git status, so file:line refs match HEAD.

**The main finding:** one catalog (lib/data/pricing-catalog.ts) is supposed to be the only source of prices, but about a dozen components still hardcode their own. The result is that the same deliverable often shows two to five different prices or scopes across pages.

**Where it hurts most:**
- **48-hour delivery.** The song pages promise it as standard. The /studio/pricing builder charges +1,400 for it, and the /book wizard has a +300 express upgrade.
- **The 4,500 'full production + video clip' card.** It lists 'video clip' and 'lyric writing' as NOT included.
- **Online pitch correction.** The page has a 'how much?' heading with no price under it.
- **Blessings.** A real derasha or bride/groom session (1-2 hours, per the site's own FAQs) has no price, because 590 covers only 30 minutes.
- **Noise removal.** It is sold at 200, 250, 350, 500 and 650.
- **Gift pages.** They show no base prices at all.

The site also leads with ex-VAT numbers when talking to families, and in places never says whether VAT applies. The decision pages are buried under 13-35 CTAs.

**Per-service rows** (service | URL | price shown | included-items clarity 0-3 | next-step clarity 0-3 | top problem):
1. Blessing (studio) | /studio/blessings | no number in its 'how much' section; button 'מ-590 + מע״מ = 696' | 1 | 1 | 590 = up to 30 min, but the pages say 30-60 min (or 1 hour for a derasha); background music has no price.
2. Bar/bat mitzvah derasha | /studio/blessings/bar-mitzvah | FAQ only: 'מתחילה מ-590' | 1 | 1 | 'Help with wording' contradicts 'text writing not included'; 1-2 hour sessions have no price.
3. Bride/groom blessing | /studio/blessings/bride-groom-blessing | FAQ only: 'מ-590, final price by text length' | 1 | 1 | Hero says background music is included; the body says it costs extra.
4. Remote blessing (phone) | only on /pricing as 'הקלטה מרחוק' 590 | none on the blessings hub | 1 | 1 | The hub describes the option but never prices it.
5. Ready song / cover | /studio/recording-song-modiin | hero 'מ-990 ₪' (no VAT); cards 990 + VAT = 1,168 | 2 | 1 | The main WhatsApp button reads 'מ-כרגע: מ-990'; who supplies the playback and session length are unclear.
6. Song Pro | /studio/pricing | 1,480 + VAT | 1 | 1 | Unclear difference from 990 (both include pitch correction); mix/master not listed.
7. Song + studio clip | /studio/pricing 1,950; /studio/blessings/video-clip has no price | 1 | 1 | The clip page's only price CTA is the 590 blessing.
8. All-In life story | /studio/pricing | 2,380 + VAT | 1 | 2 | 'הפקה מלאה' is never defined.
9. Full production + video clip | /studio/recording-song-modiin | 4,500 + VAT | 0 | 1 | Card says the clip and writing are NOT included.
10. Single production | /studio/pricing | 3,500 + VAT | 2 | 2 | The add-on 'external mix' at 1,750 contradicts the 500 online mix.
11. Bat-mitzvah clip | /studio/blessings/bat-mitzvah-clip | 'החל מ-2,590 ₪' (no VAT) | 1 | 2 | Not in the catalog; the blog says 2,590 is audio-only.
12. Studio half hour / hour | /studio/pricing | 750 / 1,500 + VAT | 2 | 2 | The builder opens on 750 room-only, which is more than the 590 blessing with editing.
13. Mobile studio | /studio/mobile-studio | 2,500 ex VAT + area fee | 1 | 2 | Hours and editing are undefined (editing 'extra', no price).
14. Session clip | song page | 450 / 750 + VAT | 2 | 2 | OK.
15. Gifts / vouchers | /studio/recording-song-modiin/gifts, /matanot | no base prices; packaging +199/+399; voucher anchored to 750 | 1 | 1 | The buyer cannot price a gift; one-year validity is a legal risk.
16. Funny ringtone | /studio/recording-song-modiin/gifts/funny-ringtone | 'מבצע ₪299' | 2 | 2 | VAT unstated; permanent 'sale'; not in the catalog.
17. Singer amplification | /events/equipment/singer-amplification | 2,800 / 5,800 / 7,800 (VAT unstated in cards) | 2 | 2 | Hours per package missing; copy says 'בלי מחירים'.
18. Online vocal fix | /online/vocal-fix | 250 + VAT per 5 min | 2 | 2 | Its own upsells (noise / volume / EQ at 500) cost double for less.
19. Noise / volume / EQ | /online/vocal-fix/* | from 500 + VAT | 2 | 2 | Five different noise-removal prices site-wide.
20. Online pitch correction | /online/vocal-fix/pitch-correction | none (only '+100 above 4 min') | 2 | 1 | The heading 'כמה זה עולה?' has no price, and the linked price list doesn't include the service.
21. Online mix and master | /online/vocal-fix/mixing | 500 + VAT | 3 | 2 | Catalog and studio add-on say 1,750; extra revision 100 here vs 580 in the studio.
22. Send file | /online/vocal-fix/send-file | none | 0 | 1 | Legal wall, then an off-site Google Form, then WhatsApp.
23. Voice cloning | /online/voice-cloning | 2,500 / 1,200 / 450 + VAT | 2 | 2 | Typo 'קlip'; otherwise clear.
24. Photo enhance | /online/vocal-fix/photo-enhance | 50 per photo, 350 for 10 (VAT not stated in the block) | 3 | 2 | Catalog says 250 for 10.
25. AI music | /academy/ai-music | 'מ־350 ₪' hint | 0 | 1 | No defined product.
26. /pro | /pro | 'החל מ-X לפני מע״מ' | 2 | 2 | Matches the catalog; lowest risk in scope.

found.notes:
Method: I fetched every in-scope live page with curl from https://yakircohen.com on 2026-10-02, turned the HTML into plain text, and pulled the JSON-LD with python3. Code facts are from the working tree at HEAD 0d163c8; `git status --short` showed no changes when I ran it.

What I could not verify:
- The /book studio wizard and the /studio/pricing builder render in the browser, not in the server HTML, so I couldn't see them interactively. The /book findings (express +300, songwriting 500, add_clip 2,500, savings claims) come from code paths (studio-recording-booking.ts, studio-upgrade-display.ts, pricing-addon-adapter.ts), not from what a visitor sees. The builder's default 885 result does appear in the live server HTML.
- I couldn't confirm whether the 'recording_basic' / 'recording_premium' entries in booking-calculator-services.ts are shown anywhere live. ClipsBookingForm imports SERVICES, but I didn't trace which ids it renders, so I left those entries out of the findings.

Legal points (section 17ד on total-price display, section 14ח on voucher validity) are flagged as risks to confirm with a lawyer. The sources are Nevo and Wikisource as summarised by WebFetch, so they are not legal advice. Two of the external quotes in the evidence are those WebFetch summaries, not verbatim text from the statute pages.

The GA4 CSV covers the old www site in 2025, so treat S37 as directional.

The live gallery placeholder (S40) is still there although commit b7da505 says such placeholders were removed; it may not be deployed yet.

The mix-price contradiction already found in commit 41b2e77 is not repeated. S10 covers only how it shows up on live pages.

A song-page testimonial cites '3 שעות אולפן, עריכה ומיקס כלולים' for a bar-mitzvah. A buyer cannot tell whether 3 hours costs 990 or 1,480.

The site makes conflicting 'final price' promises. /book says 'המחיר שמוצג הוא המחיר הסופי' (studio-recording-booking.ts:485-486), while the blessing FAQ says 'מחיר סופי לפי אורך הטקסט' (services.ts:1047), the global FAQ says 'המחיר הסופי תלוי במורכבות', and every quote button says 'כרגע' (pricing-catalog.ts:798-816).

Unrelated upsells crowd out the base offer. On the blessing and song+clip pages the only price block besides the 590 CTA is an events cross-sell, 'אטרקציה מ-1,695 ₪ לפני מע״מ' (heavy smoke or wedding photography), shown before any blessing or clip package price. /book hides express from families. The 300 'express' upgrade is offered only in the pro path (cover/original/voiceover); event songs and blessings, the 48-hour-sensitive buyers, never see an express option or price. Source: studio-recording-booking.ts:428-450.

The live site is behind HEAD, which affects verification and any 'already fixed' claims. Commit b7da505 (today) removed the 'גלריה בקרוב' block (components/services/ServicePortfolioMedia.tsx:66 comment), but live /studio/blessings/bat-mitzvah-clip still shows 'גלריה בקרוב / אנחנו מעלים דוגמאות נוספות לעמוד זה'. found.summary:
Events offer and price clarity audit. Sources: the live site (fetched 2026-10-02) and HEAD 0d163c8. For every file cited here the working tree matched HEAD (git status was clean for those paths).

Bottom line: the attraction price ladder (1,695 / 3,051 / 4,322 / from 5,424 ex VAT) is the only events price that holds steady across pages. Everything else a couple or parent shops for first is broken in one of three ways: it has no price, it has a different price in two or more places, or it is anchored to the wrong number. That covers the DJ, DJ plus attractions, the wedding and bar mitzvah packages, the festival package, LED, sound rental, host, event video, slideshow packages and vouchers.

The four worst problems:
1. /book tells DJ shoppers the DJ starts at 2,000 including VAT. Every DJ page says 5,900.
2. The DJ calculator on /events/dj-events prices Yakir personally at 9,800 plus VAT. The FAQ on the same page says 8,305 plus VAT, which is 9,800 total.
3. The central /pricing page has no row for the DJ, the festival package, photography, sound rental, LED or the host.
4. The attractions booking wizard shows a "promo" second activation at 1,400 crossed out from 1,750. The real add-on price shown on the same site is 1,200.

found.notes:
Method: the live pages were fetched with curl and the visible text extracted, filtering out repeated footer and testimonial blocks; JSON-LD was parsed from the same HTML. Code facts come from `git show HEAD:<path>`. `git status --short` on every cited file returned nothing, so the working tree matched HEAD for all of them.

Not verified:
- The promo upsell (OE-03) and the other strings inside the lazily loaded EventsBookingWizard chunk could not be found in the live JS by statically scanning the chunks referenced from /book and /book/events. The DJ calculator strings (OE-02) were confirmed live in /_next/static/chunks/0gwnvikka.lss.js.
- The raw numbers that appear next to price cards (e.g. "150005 שעות DJ", "1695") are sr-only and aria-hidden `<data>`/`<time>` elements. They are not visible, so they are not reported.
- I did not POST, submit or interact with any form or wizard. Wizard behaviour comes from the code.
- Legal point: the external source (dinolaw) says the duty to show VAT-inclusive prices for services covers only listed sectors, so showing before-VAT event prices is presented as a clarity issue rather than a clear legal violation. The fake-reference-price issue (OE-03) is flagged by the repo's own comment and by Consumer Protection Law s.2(a) per hflaw.co.il.
- The attractions calculator data (lib/data/attractions-calculator.ts) is not rendered by any live component except via event-index-attractions-pro.ts. Its GEO_FEES are used only as evidence that travel numbers exist.

found.summary:
Scope: 31 sellable services and pages across /podcast/*, /business/*, /voiceover/*, /video (excluding events), audiobooks, transcription and video presentation. I fetched each page live on 2026-10-02 and checked it against HEAD 0d163c8. `git status --porcelain` came back empty, so the working tree matches HEAD for every file cited.

Bottom line: the podcast offer contradicts itself on almost every page, so a customer who writes in still doesn't know what they're buying.
- The hero, the meta description and the FAQ say a "ready-to-upload episode from 750". On the same page, 750 is a raw 30-minute recording with no editing.
- The same 4K video episode costs 1,650 on /podcast and 2,500 on /podcast/podcast-recording.
- On most podcast pages, the "book online" button shows a price that belongs to a different product: 950 on most pages, and 650 or 2,500 where the price is right but the product isn't in the wizard. It then opens a /book wizard that doesn't contain that page's product.
- B2B gaps:
  - The business voiceover links go to a DJ voice-tag page.
  - Voiceover, corporate video, conference presentations, the A-to-Z podcast production and the grandpa podcast have no price at all.
  - Business podcast's custom tier shows "0 ₪".

Per-service table (service | URL | price shown | what's included, 0-3 | next step, 0-3 | top problem):
1. Podcast hub | /podcast | 750 / 950 / 1,650 + VAT; FAQ also says 4K "from 2,500" | 1 | 1 | "ready episode from 750" is raw; 1,650 vs 2,500 clash
2. Recording only, half hour | /podcast table, /pricing | 750 + VAT | 1 | 1 | called "ready episode" in hero, meta, FAQ and /book; called raw everywhere else
3. Audio podcast package | /podcast, /pricing, /book | 950 + VAT | 2 | 2 | no dedicated page; 1 hour with editing is cheaper than 1 hour of room time
4. Video podcast | /podcast, /pricing, /book | 1,650 + VAT | 1 | 1 | same deliverables sold for 2,500 elsewhere; /pricing lists no editing
5. Full production | /podcast/podcast-recording | 2,500 + VAT = 2,950 | 2 | 1 | book button shows 950 and the wizard has no 2,500 package
6. A-to-Z production | /podcast/podcast-production | none | 1 | 2 | no price, yet linked as "video podcast" and as the 2,500 item
7. Content package | /pricing, /book | 2,800 | 1 | 1 | no page explains it
8. Podcast editing | /podcast/podcast-editing | 750 per raw hour | 3 | 2 | turnaround given as 24-48h, 2-5 days and 24h; CTA shows 950
9. Studio rental | /podcast/podcast-studio-modiin | 750 / 1,500 (FAQ only) | 1 | 1 | no price block; labels say "self-service" and "ready episode"
10. Self-service studio | /podcast/self-service-studio | 650 per hour | 2 | 1 | CTA "from 650" opens a wizard with no 650 option
11. Mobile podcast | /podcast/mobile-podcast-at-home | from 2,500 | 1 | 1 | editing included? the wizard adds 2,500 on top of a package
12. Grandpa podcast | /podcast/podcast-with-grandpa | none | 2 | 1 | CTA shows 950; the events wizard prices it at 1,695
13. Bulk production | /podcast/bulk-production | 950 per episode | 2 | 1 | 4-episode monthly minimum not costed; is recording included?
14. Studio in a box | /podcast/studio-in-a-box | 2,500 | 1 | 1 | editing for 10 episodes has no defined scope
15. Business podcast | /podcast/corporate-podcast | 6,500 / 4,800 per month / "0 ₪" | 2 | 2 | 0 ₪ tier; "weekly" vs 2 episodes a month

evidence.excerpt: 'הצעה לפי פרויקט + מע״מ' followed by 'פרטי התשלום אינם נשמרים באתר, והסליקה מתבצעת דרך ספק מאושר.' (repeated under each of 16 cards)

items.fix_proposal: Show the payment line only where online payment exists. Elsewhere, say what happens next ('שולחים הודעה, מקבלים הצעה בכתב ותאריך'). File: the hub card component used on /business and /podcast.
items.owner_question: Can customers pay online for any business service today, or is everything invoiced after a quote?

items.title: Data: podcast, business and voiceover pages bring little traffic, so each lead counts
items.customer_impact: With only dozens of views per service page per year, every confused visitor is a large share of potential B2B revenue, so clarity fixes here pay off per lead rather than through volume.

evidence.excerpt: 2025: podcast studio rental 91 views; social media 77; 'הפקת פודקאסט וידאו ... החל מ-₪2500' 64; voiceover services 35 (of 4,816 active users)

items.fix_proposal: Prioritise PB-01 to PB-05 (clarity and booking path) over new pages. Once GA4 key events are set, track WhatsApp clicks per package to see which offer converts.
items.owner_question: Roughly how many podcast, voiceover and business leads a month do you get today, and how many of them close? (This sets which fixes matter most.)

owner_questions: Podcast 750 half-hour: raw file only, or basic editing included? Should the headline price be the cheapest finished episode (950)?
Video podcast 1,650 vs full production 2,500: same service or different? If different, what does 2,500 add, and which should stay?
Mobile podcast 2,500: is editing included? How many recording minutes does it cover? Is it the total price or a surcharge on top of the 950/1,650 package? What does video add?
Grandpa podcast: prices for podcast only, song only, and the full package (video, gallery, private page)?
Voiceover: price for one IVR message, a 30-second ad, and one minute of narration? Are usage rights included? Is Yakir the only narrator?
What is the real price of the 5-sentence DJ set voiceover: 590 or 1,200?
Per-hour logic: what should room-only, room + technician, recording + editing, editing-only and overtime cost? Is 950 for an edited 1-hour episode meant to be cheaper than 1,500 for a 1-hour room?
A-to-Z podcast production: how do you price it (season, month or episode), and what did recent clients pay?
Business podcast: retainer 2 episodes a month or weekly? Is office recording included? What does it add over bulk production at 950 per episode? Is there a 'from' price for the custom tier?
Bulk production: is studio recording included in 950? Maximum episode length? Is the 4-episode monthly minimum firm?
Studio in a box: length and editing level for each of the 10 included episodes?
Content studio retainer 4,500: how many reels, and why is it better value than the 2,800 one-off?
On-site retainer 28,000: is editing included, and how much? How many episodes should a half day produce?
HR retainer 18,500: how many videos a month, and how long? What does editing the onboarding-day footage cost?
Audiobooks: is 750 per recorded hour or per finished hour? Is ACX mastering included? Narrator fee? Discount for studio days?
Corporate video and business video presentations: typical 'from' price or range?
Corporate songs 5,000: are lyrics written? Who sings? Audio branding: who voices it, how many revisions, what turnaround, what music license?
Do 4- and 8-episode podcast bundles with 15-20% savings exist (promised on 4 city pages)? Prices?
What does an extra revision round cost (the site says 'symbolic'; the catalog says 580)?
What turnaround can you promise for full production, the audio episode, editing only and voiceover?
Which lead channel should be primary for podcast and business: WhatsApp, the /book wizard or the callback form?
Is the 200 one-off social edit vs the 950 single promo reel intentional? Should the social-media packages appear on /pricing?
Can any business service be paid online today?
How many recording spaces and cameras do you actually have (3 or 4 spaces; 2-3 or 3 cameras)?
How many podcast, voiceover and business leads do you get per month, how many close, and what do customers ask first when they contact you?

The /book wizard was opened in the browser pane by loading pages only. Nothing was clicked, typed or submitted. Verified live:
- The 2,500 banner appears while the 950 package is marked as selected (full production).
- Step 1 shows '1,121 ₪ סופי' under a 2,500 banner (mobile).

Comes from the code only, not checked live:
- Mobile total at step 2: package + 2,500 + region fee (PodcastBookingWizard.tsx:358-382). I'd have had to click to see it.

Odd behaviour I didn't count as a finding: on the first load, the browser tab ended up on /events/dj-events once. I couldn't reproduce it.

The wizard showed 'שחזרנו טיוטה שמורה' (a saved draft was restored). It came from earlier browser-pane storage, not from me.

found.summary:
Scope covered: /academy and all 10 /academy/* pages, /voiceover/course, /clinic, /stuttering and /courses (a 308 redirect to /academy). Every page was fetched live on 2026-10-02 and checked against the code at HEAD 0d163c8. The working tree was clean, so the code matches HEAD.

Main finding: the academy has one clear price list (on the /academy hub), but the course pages people land on show no course price at all. Two pages show a wrong price, and the stuttering offer is described in four contradicting ways with no price.

- /voiceover/course shows 'from 590' (the blessing-recording price) and its booking button opens the studio wizard.
- The DJ, music-production, voiceover and AI course pages only say 'contact us'. In the 2025 GA4 data the DJ course was the most-viewed academy page.
- A 90-minute DJ, production or voiceover lesson has three prices: 1,280, 1,470, and 'from 990' on the course pages.
- The Hebrew-lesson plans contradict themselves: the annual plan is 36 lessons in one place and 48 in another, and 12 x 3,200 is 38,400, against 11,520 for the year.
- The stuttering offer is called 'therapy' on one page and 'not therapy' on another. The hub price is 1,200 per hour, while the NeverMind site those pages link to shows 750.
- The three academy testimonials started life as placeholders.
- On /pricing, the workshop booking links open the private-lesson wizard.

Per-service table (service | URL | price shown | what's included, 0-3 | next step, 0-3 | top problem):
1. Academy hub | /academy | 12 price points, all before VAT | 2 | 1 | Too many overlapping prices, and five different CTAs.
2. Private lesson 60/90 | /academy/private-lessons | 990 / 1,280 + VAT, exact | 2 | 2 | Hero says '90 minutes'. FAQ says prices are on the booking page. Book first, then WhatsApp.
3. DJ course | /academy/dj-course | None on the page (hub shows 1,470 per 90 min) | 2 | 1 | No course price, number of lessons or total cost. 'Full track' and 'youth track' are never defined.
4. DJ + AI | hub card that links to /academy/dj-course | None | 0 | 1 | Duplicate card with no page of its own.
5. Music production | /academy/music-production | Book button 'from 990'. FAQ says 'contact us' | 2 | 2 | No package price for a course of '2-3 months, weekly'.
6. AI music course | /academy/ai-music | Course: none. Services: 'from 350' | 1 | 1 | Mixes a course with links to services. Course scope and price unknown.
7. Voiceover course | /academy/voiceover | Book button 'from 990'. FAQ says 'contact us' | 2 | 2 | No price for a 3-6 month course. Conflicts with item 8.
8. Frontal voiceover course | /voiceover/course | 'From 590' (the blessing price) | 1 | 1 | Wrong price, wrong booking wizard, and syllabus only by WhatsApp.
9. Stuttering course | /academy/stuttering-course | None | 1 | 2 | No price or number of sessions. Calls itself a 'therapeutic program'.
10. NeverMind session | hub card | 1,200 + VAT per 60 min | 1 | 1 | The linked nevermind.co.il shows 750 per 60 min.
11. Clinic | /clinic | None | 1 | 2 | Says 'the goal is not to treat stuttering'. No price.
12. Stuttering support | /stuttering | None | 1 | 1 | H1 is 'stuttering therapy'. Three paths, none priced.
13. Hebrew lessons | /academy/ulpan | 500 / 3,200 / 11,520, VAT not mentioned | 2 | 3 | 36 vs 48 lessons, a 70% gap between monthly and annual, no lesson length.
14. Hebrew lessons, English | /academy/hebrew-lessons | Same prices | 2 | 3 | Same contradictions, plus a 3-month outcome promise.
15. Acoustic / home-studio consulting | /academy/home-studio | 500 / 950 + VAT | 2 | 2 | Travel fee undefined. Hub card shows no price.
16. Team workshops | /academy/workshops | 2,800 / 6,500 / 7,500 before VAT | 2 | 2 | Shown as both fixed and 'from'. Group size 12 vs 5-15. /pricing books them in the lesson wizard.
17. Sound Lab (parent and child) | hub only | 1,500 + VAT per 60 min | 1 | 1 | No page. Card says 'weekly' but the price is per session.
18. Master monthly | hub only | 3,920 per month | 2 | 1 | Saves only 40 a month compared with single lessons.
19. Pro-Partnership | hub only | 21,500 | 2 | 1 | The '2,300 saving' does not add up.

found.summary:
The catalog in lib/data/pricing-catalog.ts is mostly respected on /pricing. Away from it, the same service often has two or three different prices. The worst cases:

1. The DJ calculator treats Yakir's VAT-inclusive DJ price (9,800) as a before-VAT price. It adds VAT again and shows a "final" 11,564 ₪.
2. The podcast hub, its meta description, its FAQ and the /book card all sell "a ready, edited episode from 750 ₪". In the catalog, 750 ₪ buys half an hour in the room with no editing.
3. The online audio fixes have conflicting price ladders: noise removal at 200, 250, 350 or 500; mixing at 500 or 1,750; pitch correction at 250 or 300.
4. The old attraction price (1,750) still shows on /events, in the /events schema and as a struck-through "was" price in the booking wizard.
5. Blog posts set out as "our 2026 price list (before VAT)" quote prices the catalog doesn't have. The main song-price article says a cover song costs 1,200, but the catalog says 990.

Other gaps:
- Bat mitzvah clip, video/clip, mobile studio, gift voucher and voiceover each have conflicting prices or no real price.
- /pricing has no DJ, photography, festival, mobile studio, video or voiceover prices.
- Most prices lead with the before-VAT figure. Israeli consumer law (section 17D) requires advertised consumer prices to be the full price including VAT. Several pages give no VAT basis at all.
- The price audits pass all of this. audit:prose-prices only checks catalog values that changed against origin/main, only matches numbers with a thousands comma, and treats the 1,750 mixing price as "explained".

found.summary:
The site loses leads after people decide to reach out. On most forms the backup copy of the lead never reaches the owner, while the visitor is told it was sent. Almost every form ends by opening WhatsApp with a long pre-filled message, so a lead exists only if the visitor actually presses Send in WhatsApp.

1. Backup lead email is rejected on 17 submit paths. The browser adds a link ("קישור להזמנה: https://yakircohen.com/book/...", "קישור: https://yakircohen.com/pricing?ask=...", "הכנה לאולפן: https://...") to the text it sends to /api/lead-notify. The server's spam rule rejects any text containing "https://" with a 400 error, before the lead is saved or emailed. Affected: the /contact quiz, the /pricing inquiry form, the /book smart form, all category wizards, 3 calculators and 3 SEO forms.
2. The visitor always sees a success message ("הפרטים נשלחו בהצלחה", "קיבלנו את הפנייה"), whatever the server answered.
3. Duplicate detection marks the real lead as "spam" and sends no email in two cases: when a draft was already auto-saved (pricing form), or when a partial "ghost" lead was already sent (studio/events/podcast/singer wizards). In the ghost case, the owner's only email says the customer did not send WhatsApp.
4. An operator-only panel ("למפעיל (מקומי בלבד) ... פתח ב-CLOSER עם הליד") is shown to every customer on the success screen. Its link leads to a 404.
5. window.open is called with "noopener", which per MDN always returns null. So every successful WhatsApp open is treated as blocked: on /, /contact and /pricing the site tab also navigates away to wa.me, and on /book a false "הדפדפן חסם את וואטסאפ" message appears.
6. The customer's own WhatsApp message contains internal CRM text: "[YC:...]" tags, "🚨 ליד פרימיום" and third-person intent lines.

Price before contact: /book cards and the smart form use the catalog. But the DJ calculator charges 9,800 before VAT for Yakir's personal DJ, while the FAQ on the same live page says 8,305 + VAT = 9,800. Its "special price for event customers" song add-on (1,500) is above the regular song price (990). The /contact quiz takes 4 steps and never shows a price.

After submitting, the customer gets nothing in writing with the service and price. The contact quiz and the quick-intake wizard collect an email address but never pass it to the server. The auto-reply only says "within 12/24 business hours" and adds portfolio links, while the site elsewhere promises "within an hour" and "within minutes".

Tracking cannot measure leads today. Three main forms (homepage callback, /pricing, /book quick intake) fire no GA4 lead event at all. The other events fire when WhatsApp opens, not when the server confirms the lead. Whether GA4 key events were configured is unknown.

found.notes:
Read-only run: no files written (plan mode was also active), no POSTs, no forms submitted, .env.local not read. All cited files were checked equal to HEAD 0d163c8 (git diff --quiet HEAD showed no difference for lead-email-notify, lead-notify route, form-validation, ingest, duplicate, PricingInquiryForm, ContactPageContent, BookingSuccessPanel, useLeadSubmit), and the working tree was clean at the time of reading.

Live checks were GET only: page HTML text, 71 production JS chunks crawled for strings, the closer link (404), wa-fallback-link presence per page, the CSP header (Koalendar allowed, report-only), and /api/lead-notify GET (404 in production as designed).

What could not be verified without a POST: that the production server code includes the isLeadSpam(body) check (it is in git since c1dbb58, 2026-06-11, and the matching client strings are live), and the actual Vercel env values. Those are owner questions.

LF-05 (window.open noopener) comes from the MDN spec plus the code; it was not reproduced in a browser.

Contact entry points mapped:
- Homepage CallbackLeadForm: 1 step; name and phone required, service and need optional. Also used on online, podcast, geo-DJ and event-index pages.
- /contact quiz: 4 steps (service, timing, level, then name*/phone*/email/message), plus tel and wa.me links.
- /pricing PricingInquiryForm: 3 steps (section*, optional row; qualify fields and message; name*/phone*/email).
- /book has several flows:
  - audience route cards (WhatsApp, with a contactless mirror email)
  - smart form: 2 steps, name* plus phone-or-email*, terms*
  - needs-discovery flow: WhatsApp only, with the Hold step
  - quick-intake wizard: 3 steps, contact first, terms*, posts to /api/lead-intake
  - category wizards under /book/[category], with ghost leads
  - Koalendar modal ('ייעוץ חינמי 15 דקות') in BookingSummaryActions and the podcast wizard
- Floating buttons: WhatsApp FAB (generic text), FAQ chat widget, send-file FAB (/online), accessibility toggle. MobileStickyCta shows pricing / booking / service hub and is hidden on /contact, /book and /pricing.

Owner side: Resend email with a score card. Score 80 or more adds '[דחוף]' to the subject and an optional ADMIN_WHATSAPP_ALERT webhook ping. Leads are stored in Upstash for 90 days; /admin/leads shows the last 150. A daily 07:00 UTC cron reminds the owner about unopened leads older than 24h.

Customer side: at most two generic emails, and only when an email reached ingest. The contact quiz and quick-intake never pass one.

verdicts.reason: The code chain is solid at HEAD, and the live client bundle builds the same body. The client adds 'קישור להזמנה: https://yakircohen.com/book/...' whenever crossSell yields offers. Every one of the 9 categories yields at least one offer. The server runs isLeadSpam(body) on that assembled body, and the URL regex matches it, so the result is a 400 before ingestLead ever runs. found.summary:
A new visitor can't tell what Yakir Cohen mainly sells, or how much the big-ticket service costs, within the first few seconds. The homepage reads like a recording-studio page ("אולפן הקלטות במודיעין - פודקאסט, שירים ואירועים"). Its main button is "book a recording". The 2025 GA4 data shows most visitors were families planning a wedding or bar/bat mitzvah.

The most damaging fact is a price mismatch. The hero, the quick-path card and the WhatsApp router all say "DJ from 1,695 ₪ + VAT" (2,000 ₪). That number is the price of one attraction. The DJ page and the same homepage say a team DJ costs 5,000 + VAT (5,900 ₪). The WhatsApp message the site writes for the customer even says "we saw from 2,000 ₪". On top of that, the central price list (/pricing) has no DJ prices at all. Podcast is shown at both 750 and 950 on the same page.

Trust is being worn down in five ways:
- **Testimonials:** they can't be checked. One identical quote was re-attributed from "אורי מזרחי" to "דניאל גרין" a day after it was written. The site's own quotes appear by default right under the "4.9 Google, 241+ reviews" badge, so they read as Google reviews.
- **Conflicting numbers:** the homepage says 5,000+ clients and 4.9, the contact page says 500+ projects and 5.0, and another homepage section says "dozens of events".
- **Fake scarcity and urgency in the booking wizards:** a fixed line "next month is full - join the waitlist", a 5-minute "your price is held" countdown that quietly restarts, made-up "checking availability" loading messages, and "was" prices that were never charged.
- **Promo banner:** the first thing on every page promises a free BTS clip and a free first podcast edit. Neither offer appears on the pages it links to.
- **Mobile first screen:** it opens with an empty 65px strip. Five floating buttons follow, and one of them sits on top of the main button.

Contact details are consistent everywhere (phone, address, opening hours, schema), which is a real strength. Production mobile Lighthouse is 72, against 95 measured locally. The page sends 622 KB of raw HTML and 589 KB of compressed JS. GA4 is preloaded even though the project's own speed report says it was removed.

The fix: open with three doors (wedding, bar/bat mitzvah, studio recording), each with one honest price including VAT. Back it with real Google reviews. Remove every fake signal. Cut the homepage from seven different service groupings down to one.

found.notes:
Method: I read the code at HEAD with git show. `git diff --stat HEAD` was empty for every file I cite, so the working tree matched HEAD. I checked the live site with curl GET only, plus a Browser-pane visit to https://yakircohen.com/ at 375x812 with JavaScript measurements; the viewport was reset to desktop afterwards. No forms, leads or WhatsApp were triggered.

One temporary file was written, home.html, under the allowed scratchpad path scratchpad/sales/first-impression-trust/. After that, plan mode was noticed and no other files were created.

What could not be verified:
- The live Google rating and review count (4.9 / 241). Google Maps needs JavaScript; I only confirmed that the maps link resolves to the place 'יקיר כהן הפקות - אולפן הקלטות במודיעין'.
- The GA4 2025 figures come from the previous site version (the page titles differ from today's).

Widgets checked and found real, harmless or not first-impression issues:
- LiveVisitorCount uses real GA4 realtime data, but production returns configured:false, so it is hidden.
- The LiveStatusProjectTicker counts are real playlist counts.
- TimeGreeting in the header is compact (greeting only, no 'LIVE' label).
- BusinessOpenBadge correctly reads the shared hours. It uses the visitor's own time zone (see FIT-12).
- EphemeralPulse on '/' only shows the general entry.
- Coupon offers (lib/data/coupon-offers.ts) are only applied via ?coupon= in /book. Nothing displays them site-wide, so they are not a first-impression issue. The default code 'YAKIR10' is a 50 ₪ discount labelled 'הטבה לזמן מוגבל', valid until 31 Dec 2026.

Overlap with other dimensions: the pricing and process agents may also report FIT-01, FIT-03 and FIT-11. Merge them by evidence.

found.summary: The only behaviour data on record is about the old WordPress site, not the new one. It is a 2025 GA4 snapshot covering 4,816 users, 87% of them from Google organic, and it recorded zero key events. There is also a June 2026 Search Console coverage export. I classified the 373 page titles by keyword (approximate). Informational pages took 50.9% of 6,692 views, service pages 36.2%, home/about 6.9% and price guides 2.3%. Wedding and bar/bat-mitzvah song lists and guides alone took 44% of all views. The two biggest family pages, a bat-mitzvah song list and a bar-mitzvah speech guide, have no equivalent on the new site. Live checks today found that all 89 unique Hebrew legacy URLs in the GSC export return 404. The redirect map holds about 214 Hebrew entries, but they do not fire on the live site: a mapped entry like /תקליטן-לחתונות gives 404, while English ones redirect. Of the 1,000 'crawled - not indexed' URLs, 77.5% are WooCommerce ?add-to-cart variants, and these now loop: they redirect 308 to themselves. The owner's local quoting tool (yakir-closer) still loads the old attraction prices from 20.8.2026: 1,750/3,200/4,450/5,500 plus the deleted 1,500 single effect. The site shows 1,695/3,051/4,322/5,424. On decisions: many owner pricing decisions are recorded with quotes (attractions ladder, DJ package, photography, hours, trust numbers, force-majeure refund, studio overlay). The DJ package decision (4 hours, up to 300 guests, 5,000) is not live: the page still shows 'personal quote', 5h/150 and 7h/300. Earlier plans already said the main CTA has no price and only the DJ page explains what drives price. Those items are still open, and the price CTA renders garbled ('מ-כרגע: מ-'). There is no lead-count, close-rate, lead-source or customer-question data anywhere in the repo or docs. The lead export removes the landing page, UTM and message fields, and leads expire after 90 days. Most WhatsApp contacts never reach the lead store. No document states the owner's ideal customer, margins or priority services. Since July, git history shows CRO changes but no measured effect.

It does not describe the current Next.js site, which was live by late May 2026 per the GSC crawl of /_next assets on 2026-05-29. (2) The commercial vs informational split is a keyword classification of 373 page titles (the snapshot has titles, not URLs), done in an inline node script with no file saved. Treat the percentages as approximate. (3) GA4 city comes from network location; the city figures are directional only, and this was not verified. (4) The GSC table has 1,000 data rows plus a header (1,001 lines), not 999. Classification: 775 add-to-cart, 44 other query strings, 73 WP archive/feed/product/tag/pagination/static, 90 legacy Hebrew content, 18 current or English slugs. The export is from about 9 June 2026 and predates the 2.10 deploy. (5) All live checks are GET-only, run 2026-10-02 against https://yakircohen.com, with no forms touched. verdicts.reason: The main claim holds and the real problem is bigger than reported. Every Hebrew redirect in the map is dead on production, and Hebrew legacy URLs return 404. The counts are wrong, though. I reproduced the same GET check (redirect: manual) and found 195 unique Hebrew content paths, not 89. All 195 return 404. Of those, 68 are already in the map (not 7) and 127 are unmapped (not 82). The remaining Hebrew paths are /product, /tag and /category (116, correctly 410) and /2019-/2020 (4, which 308 to /blog). One framing problem: טבלה.csv is the GSC 'crawled - currently not indexed' report (מטא נתונים.csv: 'נסרק - לא נכלל באינדקס כרגע'). These URLs are by definition not in Google results, so 'clicks an old Google result' does not apply to them. The damage is through external links, bookmarks and shares, and through ranking that is not recovered. The 87% figure is 2025 first-user source for the old site, not traffic to these specific URLs. Critical severity is still defensible, because the entire 214-entry Hebrew redirect layer, including /מחירון, does nothing in production.

found.summary:
I compared the site's catalog prices (lib/data/pricing-catalog.ts at HEAD 0d163c8; all prices are stored before VAT, VAT 18%) with the public prices of Israeli competitors, all fetched on 2026-10-02. Across the core family services the site's price is above every public price I found:
- Blessing: 696 ILS incl. VAT, against 147-500.
- Gift song: 1,168 ILS, against 197-900 at individual studios and 700-1,200 on the Midrag price guide.
- Bar/bat mitzvah DJ: 5,900 ILS, against 1,800-3,000 at small DJs and 2,000-5,000 on the d.co.il guide.
- Studio hour: 1,770 ILS, against 100-400.

Competitors also put things in the base price that the site charges extra for, or leaves unclear. Their blessing prices include background music, and the site calls it an extra without ever giving its price. Competitor DJ prices state that sound and lighting are included. Competitors publish group prices for gift songs; the site only lists 190 ILS + VAT per extra singer. The packages (song + clip, All-In) are within the upper part of the market range.

Voiceover has no per-spot price on the site. The voiceover pages show the blessing price (from 590 + VAT) and say "what you get: a recorded blessing".

Legal baseline, from an official gov.il document I fetched (the Attorney General's position, March 2021): section 17D of the Consumer Protection Law says a business may state a price to a consumer only as the total price, and section 17A defines the total as including VAT. The site leads with pre-VAT prices on consumer pages. That includes /events ("from 5,000 ILS before VAT", with no VAT-inclusive figure on the page) and 80 price entries in the /pricing structured data that search engines read.

Research I fetched supports showing the final price up front:
- Nielsen Norman Group: price is users' #1 information need, and they go to competitors when it is hidden.
- Baymard: 40% of checkout abandonment is "extra costs too high".
- A field experiment published in Marketing Science: cost transparency raised purchases by about 21%.
- A review in the Journal of Consumer Psychology: base price + surcharge layouts lead people to underestimate the total.
- One NBER field experiment found that hiding fees until checkout raises short-term revenue. Israeli law does not allow that for consumers anyway.

An old Google-indexed blessing product page now returns HTTP 410 with an empty body, so a searcher who clicks it sees a blank page.

items.title: Consumer pages lead with pre-VAT prices; Israeli law allows stating only the VAT-inclusive total to consumers
items.customer_impact: A family sees 590 or 5,000 on cards, in the chat bot and in search results, and later hears 696 or 5,900. That feels like a bait price. It also makes the site look more expensive than it is next to competitors who show a single final number.

evidence.ref: https://www.gov.il/BlobFolder/dynamiccollectorresultitem/9139-05-18/he/9139-05-18.pdf (Attorney General position, class action 9139-05-18, signed 4 March 2021, fetched 2026-10-02, text extracted with macOS PDFKit)
evidence.excerpt: Quotes section 17D: a business may not state a consumer price 'אלא אם כן הוא המחיר הכולל בלבד ורק במטבע ישראלי'. Section 17A defines the total price as including 'מס ערך מוסף'. Para 100: the total price must be clear and must not make the consumer do calculations.

evidence.ref: curl -sL https://yakircohen.com/events | sed -e 's/<[^>]*>/ /g' | tr -s ' ' | tr '\n' ' ' | grep -o -E '.{0,200}5,000 ₪ לפני מע״מ.{0,120}'

80 structured-data offers, e.g. 'ברכה / אמירה","description":"אולפן והקלטות","price":590,"priceCurrency":"ILS"'. 0 occurrences of valueAddedTaxIncluded. Visible cards read 'ברכה / אמירה 590 ₪ · עד חצי שעה ... 590 ₪ + מע״מ'.
'המחירים לפני מע״מ (+18%). ברכה כוללת הקלטה ועריכה בסיסית.' This text is live on /studio/blessings and /studio/recording-song-modiin (verified with curl).
Line 2: 'מקור אמת יחיד לכל מחירי השירות (לפני מע״מ)'. formatPriceLine builds 'כרגע: 750 ₪ + מע״מ 135 ₪ = 885 ₪ סופי'. formatFromPriceDual builds 'מ-X ₪ + מע״מ = Y ₪'.

evidence.ref: https://marketing.wharton.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Morwitz-Vicki-Wroe-Alderson-PAPER-JCP-2016.pdf (Greenleaf, Johnson, Morwitz, Shalev, J. Consumer Psychology 26(1), 2016, fetched 2026-10-02)

Explicitly incl. VAT: Clip Nolad (550 'כולל מע"מ'), Snoop DJ, Beit Ariela, Midrag DJ guide. Explicitly plus VAT: Li-Ron podcast, Magic Studios podcast, karyan.org.il, Yaniv Morozovsky, Spacenter listings. Most song and blessing studios do not say.

items.fix_proposal: On every consumer-facing page, show the VAT-inclusive total as the one headline number, for example 'ברכה / אמירה - 696 ₪ (כולל מע״מ)', '5,900 ₪ כולל מע״מ'. Remove the 'X ₪ + מע״מ =' layout from consumer cards. Change formatFromPriceDual / formatPriceLine in lib/data/pricing-catalog.ts so consumer formats output the total only. Add a separate business format for B2B pages and quotes. Replace the 'לפני מע״מ' copy in components/seo/BlessingsHubPageContent.tsx:202, lib/chatbot-data.ts:117/143/155, lib/data/services.ts:176/971 and the /events cards (priceAnchorExVat in lib/data/service-fit-matrix.ts:551,562). Keep pre-VAT prices only on pages aimed at businesses (/business/*). This summarises the official source; it is not legal advice, so confirm with your accountant or lawyer.

items.title: Research: showing the final price up front builds trust; hidden or extra costs drive people to competitors
items.customer_impact: When the price is unclear or grows at the end, visitors go elsewhere and trust drops. That matches the owner's complaint that people contact him without understanding the price.

evidence.excerpt: B2B study: when prices are hidden, users go to competitors' sites and see the company as evasive. When exact prices are impossible, show typical-scenario prices or ranges. Quote: 'Prospective customers want to know the price as their #1 info need'.
Hiding prices adds interaction cost, suggests the service is unaffordable, and makes the firm look dubious.

Excluding people who were 'just browsing': 40% abandon because extra costs (shipping, tax, fees) were too high, and 12% because they couldn't see or calculate the total cost up front. The fetched text did not show the survey year or sample size.

evidence.ref: https://phys.org/news/2020-04-transparency-sales.html (summary of Mohan, Buell & John, Marketing Science 39(6), 2020, fetched 2026-10-02; the INFORMS page returned 403)
evidence.excerpt: Field experiment: disclosing costs raised purchases about 21% (soup) and sales 22% (online wallets); the mechanism is trust. Quote: 'Cost transparency represents an act of intimate disclosure and fosters trust.'

evidence.ref: https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w25186/w25186.pdf (Blake, Moshary, Sweeney, Tadelis, NBER WP 25186, Oct 2018, fetched 2026-10-02)
evidence.excerpt: Counterpoint: on StubHub, showing the full price up front reduced how many tickets, and which quality, people bought; hiding fees made price comparison harder and people spent more. For Israeli consumers that practice is barred by section 17D (market-01).
Competitor Li-Ron markets its transparency: 'אנו מציגים את כל המחירים של שירותי האולפן'. Top-DJ, Lior Sound, narration.co.il and musiconhold hide prices entirely.

items.fix_proposal: On every service page, show one final VAT-inclusive price next to a short 'included / not included' list. For custom items, show a typical-scenario price or range rather than a bare 'from'. Make sure the price the customer hears on WhatsApp is the same number they saw. Files: lib/data/pricing-catalog.ts (formats and transparency lists), the pricing and service page components.

found.notes:
Method and limits:
- All competitor pages were fetched on 2026-10-02. WebSearch is US-based and not exhaustive, so the competitor sets are the ones I could find and fetch, not a full census.
- Numbers come from WebFetch summaries, which are written by a small model. I re-checked the key ones with curl on the raw HTML: Li-Ron 350 and 390; Kolot 250 and 350; Dana Malka 500; Magic 250 and 600; Snoop 1,800-2,300; Clip Nolad 550 incl. VAT; Echo 350. The rest rely on WebFetch only.
- Most competitors do not say whether their prices include VAT. Some may be עוסק פטור (VAT-exempt); I could not verify this, so comparisons with the site's VAT-inclusive totals are approximate.
- Li-Ron runs several domains (liron-music.com and three other Hebrew-IDN domains) and is counted as one competitor.
- Some competitors are outside the central area: Gozlan Mix (Ashdod), Ron Moshe (Netivot), PodSpace (Haifa, not used).
- Several competitor prices are labelled promotions with a struck-through 'regular' price (Magic, Clip Nolad, karyan). I report the price shown.

Legal source:
- gov.il HTML pages return 403 to automated fetches. The legal baseline comes from the Attorney General's position PDF hosted on gov.il, with text extracted locally via macOS PDFKit; it quotes sections 17D and 17A.
- The Consumer Protection Authority's own guidance page was not fetched. Its January 2023 pricing paper and an October 2021 news PDF were fetched but do not address VAT display.
- A 2005 Knesset research paper (fs.knesset.gov.il) confirms the 'total price in Israeli currency' duty for goods.
- This is a summary of sources, not legal advice.

Code and site:
- Code facts come from HEAD 0d163c8. `git diff --stat HEAD` showed no working-tree changes to lib/data/pricing-catalog.ts or lib/data/service-fit-matrix.ts.
- Live-site facts are from curl GETs on 2026-10-02. No forms were touched.
- Temporary PDFs were saved by the WebFetch tool under ~/.claude/projects/.../tool-results/. Nothing in the repo was modified.

verdicts.reason: The legal source checks out and pre-VAT headline prices are live on consumer pages. Two parts of the evidence are imprecise. (1) The /events page does contain 'כולל מע״מ' 8 times in the raw HTML, inside the RSC payload of a nav component. It is 0 times in the rendered text, so the claim 'grep returned nothing' is only true for the rendered text. (2) Many pages already print the total next to the base price ('590 ₪ + מע״מ = 696 ₪'). So the 'later hears 696' impact mainly applies to the /events cards, the /pricing intro, hero lines and the chatbot. Section 17D still requires 'the total price only', so the dual display is also arguably non-compliant. High severity is justified.
verdicts.evidence: Got the gov.il PDF (27 pages) as text with Swift PDFKit, in memory. It contains the 17D quote: 'לא יפרסם עוסק ולא ינקוב ... אלא אם כן הוא המחיר הכולל בלבד ורק במטבע ישראלי'. 17A defines the total price as including '(1) מס ערך מוסף, אגרות או תשלומי חובה'. Para 100: the total price 'אינו מצריך את הצרכן לבצע תחשיבים'. Rendered text of live /events: 'לפני מע״מ' x4 ('מ-5,000 ₪ לפני מע״מ' x2, 'מ-1,750 ₪ לפני מע״מ', '₪750 לפני מע״מ'), 'כולל מע״מ' x0. /pricing: 80 '"price":' offers and 0 valueAddedTaxIncluded. The intro reads 'ברכה ₪590 , שיר מוכן ₪990 , פודקאסט אודיו ₪950 - לפני מע״מ'. At HEAD: BlessingsHubPageContent.tsx:202 'המחירים לפני מע״מ (+18%)' (also live on /studio/blessings), pricing-catalog.ts:2 / 798-806 / 814-816, chatbot-data.ts:117/143/155 and services.ts:176/971 all match the quotes. found.summary:
I walked the live site at mobile width (375x812, read-only, nothing submitted) as five customers. For each one I started from the most likely Google landing page, picked by sitemap priority and how well the title matches the search, and also from the homepage. All five journeys fail in the same way. The price a visitor sees first is not the price they are quoted. The "what's included" lists are often template filler or contradict themselves. Every path ends in WhatsApp, and the contact step asks questions that have nothing to do with the customer's need.

Summary table (persona | clicks to price | price found | main blocker):

1. Bar mitzvah parent (landing /events/bar-mitzvah, priority 0.85, title "הפקת בר מצווה ובת מצווה - DJ ואטרקציות")
   - Clicks to price: DJ alone takes 1 tap on the in-page "מחירון" link, or 10.6 screens of scrolling. DJ plus attractions is never priced as a package. You need 2 more taps to /events/attractions and have to add the parts up yourself.
   - Price found: DJ 5,000 ₪ + VAT (5,900). The bundle says "הצעה בוואטסאפ".
   - Main blocker: three different DJ prices on one journey. The homepage says 1,695, /book#dj says "2,000 ₪ סופי", the service page says 5,000. The "most requested" bundle has no price.

2. Partner birthday song gift (landing /blog/recorded-song-birthday-gift or /studio/recording-song-modiin/gifts)
   - Clicks to price: in the blog post, 0 taps, but the price is only in a box at the end of the article. The gifts page shows no price; 1 tap to the song page, then scroll to screen 23 of 43.8. The homepage path "מתנות › יום הולדת" is a dead end (WhatsApp only).
   - Price found: 990 ₪ + VAT (1,168).
   - Main blocker: the gift pages show no song price. Delivery is promised as 48 hours free, 5 days, 1-2 weeks, or same day, and 48 hours is also sold as a 1,400 ₪ add-on.

3. Small business podcast (landing /podcast/podcast-studio-modiin or /podcast, both priority 0.9)
   - Clicks to price: 0 taps to a wrong "from 750". The real 950 is at screen 16.2 of 47.6. No monthly plan price exists.
   - Price found: 950 ₪ per episode. The only monthly price is the corporate 4,800 ₪ plan.
   - Main blocker: "פרק מוכן להעלאה מ-750" is false, because 750 is a raw 30-minute recording with no editing. There is no season or monthly price for a small business.

4. Wedding couple, recorded blessing (landing /studio/blessings/bride-groom-blessing)
   - Clicks to price: the "מחירון" link jumps to an empty block. The price is inside a collapsed FAQ: 2 taps.
   - Price found: 590 ₪ + VAT. The background-music add-on price appears nowhere. A couple price (1,000) appears only in a blog post.
   - Main blocker: the page header promises help with the text and background music, but the 590 product excludes both.

5. Amateur singer, online fix (landing /online/vocal-fix/pitch-correction, title "תיקון זיופים (Pitch Correction) מקצועי מרחוק")
   - Clicks to price: there is no price on the page. Its "full price list" link has no pitch-correction line. At least 2 taps to find it as an add-on on the mixing page.
   - Price found: three different numbers. 250 (only in hidden Google data), 300 (add-on), 500 (mixing).
   - Main blocker: no visible price, and a legal affidavit plus a Google Form before you can send a file.

found.notes:
How I worked: everything was read-only. I fetched live pages with curl and extracted visible text, decoding the wa.me links to read the pre-filled WhatsApp messages. I used the Claude Browser at 375x812 to measure where prices sit on the page, check sticky links and anchors, and see client-side content. I never typed into a form, submitted anything or clicked a send or WhatsApp button. No files were created. Live text is quoted from the pages. File citations are from `git show HEAD:<path>` at HEAD 0d163c8. `git status --short` returned nothing at check time, so the working tree matched HEAD when I looked, despite the note that another session was editing.

Landing pages were chosen by sitemap priority plus how well the title matches the likely search. The 2025 GA4 snapshot is from the old WordPress site, so it was only used to show that bar/bat mitzvah and chuppah content drew traffic.

Things I could not verify:
- Actual search queries and current landing traffic. There is no Search Console export with queries.
- Whether /api/lead-notify emails actually arrive.
- Whether the old Hebrew URLs still get visits. The Dropbox crawl export marks many of them as crawled but not indexed.

The root cause of the Hebrew-redirect 404s is likely an encoding mismatch, but I did not prove it.

Two observations I deliberately did not report as site bugs:
1. The shared Browser tab ("seed") navigated by itself to /book?catalog=full_podcast_production and later to mobile_podcast_at_home while I was reading other pages. Another session or the user is probably using that tab, so I moved my checks to a separate tab and closed it afterwards.
2. The DJ calculator on /events/dj-events showed only a loading skeleton in that shared tab, but rendered fully in a fresh tab after scrolling.

The "0 גולשים כרגע" text in the homepage server HTML stays invisible to users (components/marketing/LiveVisitorCount.tsx), so I did not report it.

I set the viewport back to desktop when done.

verdicts.reason: The DJ quick-form part is confirmed. It collects only date, venue and guests, and says data is 'not sent to the site server', yet mirrorWhatsAppLeadToEmail posts the text to /api/lead-notify. The callback part is overstated. The form does open WhatsApp ('מעדיפים שנחזור אליכם?', success text 'פתחנו שיח בוואטסאפ'), but submitLead also emails the name and phone to /api/lead-notify with keepalive. The owner receives the lead even if WhatsApp never opens, so the fix 'save the lead to the server' is already in place. The real defect is the UX mismatch.
verdicts.evidence: git show HEAD:components/forms/CallbackLeadForm.tsx:45 'מעדיפים שנחזור אליכם?', :48 'פתחנו שיח בוואטסאפ', :110-119 submitLead({... name, phone}, href). hooks/useLeadSubmit.ts:35 openWhatsAppLead, :41 await notifyLeadByEmailAsync. lib/lead-email-notify.ts:104-113 fetch('/api/lead-notify', {method:'POST', ..., keepalive: true}). lib/data/book-qualification-fields.ts:133 '"dj-vip": [EVENT_DATE, VENUE, GUEST_COUNT]'. BookQualificationMiniForm.tsx:162 'לא נשלח לשרת האתר'. BookAudienceCard.tsx:176-182 mirrorWhatsAppLeadToEmail; lib/mirror-whatsapp-lead.ts:24 notifyLeadByEmail. The browser on /book#dj shows the mini form with those 3 fields and the note.
verdicts.correction: The callback lead is not lost: name and phone are emailed. Report it as a UX problem (a callback request forces WhatsApp), not a server-capture gap. The DJ quick form's missing phone field and false privacy note stand.
